headline: Boxer’s Winning Strategy Involved Visualizing Opponent As A Persistent Call Center Agent
body:
The gold-medal winning pugilist revealed today that her narrow 3-2 victory in the recent Asian Games final was fueled by a novel psychological technique: imagining that her opponent was a telemarketer repeatedly calling to offer an extended warranty on her home appliance.

“Every time she threw a jab, I just heard the words ‘Sir, your plan is expiring,’” the athlete explained during a press conference. “It gave me the kind of focused, righteous indignation that you just can’t replicate in a standard gym sparring session. By the third round, I wasn’t fighting for a medal; I was fighting to be taken off the permanent ‘Do Not Call’ list.”

Her coach noted that the training regimen included hours of listening to aggressive hold music and automated voice menus to increase her heart rate and irritability before stepping into the ring. The athlete now credits this unorthodox mental conditioning for helping her maintain composure under pressure, noting that compared to the frustration of trying to reach a human representative, a world-class opponent felt remarkably polite and easy to dismiss.
caption: Forget protein shakes and heavy lifting—this is the mental edge the pros are really using to win. Would you be able to stay this calm in the ring? #AsianGames #Boxing #MentalToughness #SportsLife (satire)
